title: Fabrication of Massive Graphene Liquid Cells (mGLCs) for In Situ TEM
content: Graphene liquid cells (GLC) [1,2] are becoming increasingly important in liquid-phase transmission electron microscopy as they allow the encapsulation of a broad range of samples ranging from biological samples to nanoparticles in 30-50 nm thick liquid environments, and facilitate the observation of beam-sensitive structures, in situ reactions at resolutions approaching the atomic scale. However, the most common issues during fabrication of graphene liquid cells (GLCs) are the rupturing of the top or both the graphene monolayers during the final step of fabrication, or the wrinkling of the graphene monolayers which leads to very little liquid entrapment and poor reproducibility. To overcome this difficulty, a simple modified method was developed, based on prior reports [3], to fabricate GLCs with enormous sizes, and most importantly with a higher chance of reproducibility.
